title: Reading 3-letter words

parent.why: Blending is reading. Once the child can join sounds, they can read words they have never seen before.

parent.learn: The middle letter is usually a vowel (a, e, i, o, u).
parent.why: The vowel is the “voice” of the word: cat, bed, pig, dog, sun. Changing it changes the word: cat → cot → cut.

parent.learn: Change one letter to make a new word.
parent.why: cat → hat → hot → hop. Each change shows that every letter in a word matters.
A family shares an ending, so learning one word teaches five: cat, hat, mat, rat, bat.

ask: Read these slowly with me: c-a-t, d-o-g, s-u-n.
I'll say sounds, you say the word: p-i-g. b-u-s.
Change the c in cat to h — what word now?
Find a 3-letter word in a storybook and read it.
How many words can you make ending in -at?

rounds.t: c – a – t makes which word?
d – o – g makes which word?
s – u – n makes which word?
Change the c in “cat” to h. What is the new word?
rounds.h: Keep -at, put h in front: h-a-t, hat.

rounds.t: Change the middle letter of “pin” to a. What is the new word?
rounds.h: p-a-n: keep p and n, swap i for a.
s-i-t, sit — like “sit on a chair”.
